messages.content:
There's a Next.js e-commerce app at `/app`. Users experience visual instability issues including layout shifts and generally a bad experience.

Your job is to assess the root cause of the user experience issues by using best practices in nexts and react and fix accordingly.

## Rules

- Don't break existing functionality
- Don't change existing class names, ids or data-testid on any of the components as tests rely on them
I will list the files in `src/components` and read the main application files `src/app/page.tsx` and `src/app/layout.tsx` to get an overview of the application structure.

thoughts.subject: Analyzing Visual Instability
thoughts.description: I'm currently focused on visual instability in the Next.js e-commerce app. My initial investigation involves looking at the codebase to pinpoint layout shift contributors and user experience issues. I've begun to examine common culprits such as images lacking width and height attributes. I also suspect several other things are to blame, and I am working to narrow this down, quickly.

thoughts.subject: Investigating Potential Causes
thoughts.description: I'm now diving deeper into the root causes of visual instability. My focus has expanded to font loading issues (FOUT/FOIT), dynamic content lacking reserved space, client-side data fetching re-renders, and improper `useEffect` use. I've also identified a directory with React best practices, which I need to reference. My immediate next steps are to scrutinize the codebase, starting with `src/app/page.tsx`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, and relevant components.

toolCalls.description:
This tool executes a given shell command as `bash -c <command>`. Command can start background processes using `&`. Command is executed as a subprocess that leads its own process group. Command process group can be terminated as `kill -- -PGID` or signaled as `kill -s SIGNAL -- -PGID`.

      The following information is returned:

      Command: Executed command.
      Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
      Stdout: Output on stdout stream. Can be `(empty)` or partial on error and for any unwaited background processes.
      Stderr: Output on stderr stream. Can be `(empty)` or partial on error and for any unwaited background processes.
      Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.
      Exit Code: Exit code or `(none)` if terminated by signal.
      Signal: Signal number or `(none)` if no signal was received.
      Background PIDs: List of background processes started or `(none)`.
      Process Group PGID: Process group started or `(none)`
